h1:
Where to Stay in Mae Hong Son & Pai?
10 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Ten Mae Hong Son & Pai hotels across every budget — a riverside luxury resort and boutique bungalows on Pai's walking street, timber huts tucked in the Mae Hong Son valley, down to riverside bungalows and dorms from ฿300. Covering the two main bases: Pai and Mae Hong Son town. Starting from around ฿300–4,800/night.
introH2: 🏙️ Why does choosing the right base in Mae Hong Son & Pai matter?
introHtml: Mae Hong Son is a long, mountainous province, and its hotels cluster around two very different bases — Pai is a laid-back little town on the Pai River, packed with a walking street, cafes and places to stay at every level from dorms to luxury resorts, while Mae Hong Son town is quieter, wrapped in mountains around the Chong Kham lake, with timber-hut stays that blend into nature. Plenty of people book without deciding whether Pai or the town is their base, then spend hours driving the winding mountain road back and forth. This guide rounds up 10 Mae Hong Son & Pai hotels we picked from real reviews, across every tier, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Mae Hong Son has no rail and limited public transport in town — renting a car or motorbike is by far the easiest way around, especially if you'll move between Pai and Mae Hong Son town (the winding road has over 1,800 curves and takes around 3 hours). Daily minivans run from Chiang Mai to both Pai and the town · In Pai you can walk the walking street easily, but you'll want wheels to head out of town · Key zones in this guide: Pai town — walking street, Pai riverside, cafes · Pai outskirts — mountain views, rice fields, quieter · Mae Hong Son town — Chong Kham lake, Wat Chong Kham & Chong Klang, valley outskirts.

entries.name: Pai Village Boutique Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Pai walking street · walk everywhere
entries.addr: 88 Moo 3, Vieng Tai, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.5, and the most reviewed by far with 653 reviews — Pai Village is a cluster of timber bungalows in a garden set right on the Pai walking street, so you step out the gate and you're among the restaurants and cafes. Real reviews love the natural wooden-house feel, the little on-site farm, and a breakfast plenty of guests mention. It's central, yet once you're inside the garden it's quiet and shady.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Boutique Garden room is the best-value starter, but if there are a few of you, the Rasa Villa is far roomier · Book ahead in the cool season as a walking-street spot fills up fast.
pros: Most reviewed in the group with 653 reviews, score 9.5
On the Pai walking street, walk to restaurants and cafes
Timber bungalows in a leafy, natural garden
Breakfast that reviews mention often
cons: On the walking street, so some nights you may hear the market
Starter rooms are compact bungalows — check the room type before booking

entries.name: Reverie Siam Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Pai River · Pai town
entries.addr: 476 Moo 8, Wiang Tai, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: Reverie Siam is the most luxurious resort in this guide, scoring 9.5, set on the Pai River in town with a colonial-meets-Lanna look. Real reviews praise the lovely pool, the wide garden, and attentive service. Every room is spacious at around 50 sqm, with options that open straight onto the pool and villas with a private garden — a great fit for a special celebration or honeymoon in Pai.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If the budget stretches, the Deluxe Pool Access lets you step straight into the pool · Come in the cool season for the most comfortable weather, but book early as the resort is small.
pros: On the Pai River in town, walkable to the action
Pool and wide garden, calm luxury feel
Every room spacious at around 50 sqm
Polished service that reviews praise often
cons: The priciest in this guide — best for a special trip
Small resort, so rooms fill fast in high season

entries.name: The Quarter Pai
entries.badge: 📍 Pai town, walk to walking street
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pai town · walk to walking street
entries.addr: 245 Moo 1 Chaisongkram Road, Wiang Tai, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: The Quarter Pai is a good-value 4-star resort in the heart of Pai town, scoring 9.3 from 181 reviews with rooms from just ฿1,400. Real reviews like the roomy, clean rooms, the pool, and a location within walking distance of the Pai walking street. There's a 66 sqm family room that sleeps several — a solid choice for couples and families who want an in-town resort without a high price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The starter Superior has no view; for a little more, the Quarter Deluxe gives you a roomier garden/pool-view room and better value · Travelling as a group, go for the Family Room.
pros: Good-value 4-star resort in central Pai
Walking distance to the Pai walking street
Roomy, clean rooms with a pool
Large 66 sqm family room available
cons: Starter Superior rooms have no view
Fills up on long weekends — book ahead

entries.name: Sang Tong Huts
entries.addr: 250 Moo 11, Pang Mu, Mae Hong Son town
entries.storyHtml: Sang Tong Huts is a distinctive set of boutique timber huts on the Mae Hong Son outskirts, scoring 9.2. Real reviews love the hut designs — each one different — the quiet hillside setting, and an on-site restaurant many call excellent. It suits travellers who want to stay in Mae Hong Son town but blended into nature rather than a concrete hotel, with rooms from just ฿1,000.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a hut with a garden or hill-view balcony to get the full atmosphere · Try dinner at the on-site restaurant — many reviews rate the food.
pros: Each timber hut uniquely designed, full of character
Quiet hillside setting, blended into nature
On-site restaurant that reviews praise
Good starter price for the atmosphere you get
cons: On the outskirts — you'll want wheels for Mae Hong Son town
Timber huts are about atmosphere; amenities are simple

entries.name: The Oia Pai Resort
entries.addr: 254 Moo 1, Mae Hi, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: The Oia Pai is a boutique resort on the Pai outskirts known for its curved villas and mountain views, scoring 9.0. Real reviews love the photogenic corners — both the curved-design villas and the man-made lake on the grounds. Being on the outskirts, it's quieter than in town, and it suits anyone after a mountain-view resort feel with plenty of photo spots, from ฿1,500.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Mountain View at the starter price already gets you a hill-view balcony, but for water views go Lake View · It's on the outskirts, so wheels make getting to the walking street easier.
pros: Distinctive curved villas, photogenic throughout
Mountain views and a lake on the grounds, laid-back feel
Pai outskirts, quieter than in town
Starter price already gets a hill-view balcony
cons: On the outskirts — you'll want wheels for the walking street
The lake is a resort feature, not a natural waterway

entries.name: Pai Country Hut
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pai · on the river, near walking street
entries.addr: 240 Moo 1, Mae Hi, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: Pai Country Hut is a great-value set of timber huts on the Pai River, well reviewed with 240 reviews, scoring 9.0 with rooms from just ฿700. Real reviews love the riverside wooden-hut feel, the balconies with hammocks to laze in, and a location near the Pai walking street. There are budget fan huts and newer air-con huts, making it ideal for backpackers who want a riverside vibe on a modest budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: In Pai's cool season a fan hut is comfortable and cheaper · For air-con and a newer room, pick the King Hut · Ask for a riverside hut for the full view.
pros: Very budget-friendly starter price on the Pai River
Riverside timber huts with hammock balconies
Well reviewed with 240 reviews, score 9.0
Near the Pai walking street, walkable
cons: Starter rooms are fan huts with no air-con
Simple timber huts — more about atmosphere than luxury

entries.name: Common Grounds Pai
entries.addr: 116 Moo 3, Wiang Tai, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: Common Grounds is a social hostel in central Pai, scoring 8.8 from 198 reviews. Real reviews love the easy way you meet fellow travellers, the laid-back common areas, and air-con dorms that sleep better than many spots in Pai. It's near the walking street, easy to step out and explore, and it suits solo backpackers who want to meet new people, from just ฿350.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Solo travellers should take an air-con dorm to meet others · Couples or anyone wanting privacy can try the private fan bungalow · Dorm prices nudge up over long weekends.
pros: Social vibe — great for solo travellers meeting new people
Air-con dorms sleep better than many spots in Pai
Central location near the walking street
Very low starter price of ฿350
cons: Shared dorms — not for those wanting quiet privacy
Dorm prices rise over festivals and long weekends

entries.name: Fern Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Valley outskirts · rice fields · Mae Hong Son
entries.addr: 64 Moo 8, Pha Bong, Mae Hong Son town
entries.storyHtml: Fern Resort is an eco resort in a valley on the Mae Hong Son outskirts, well reviewed with 602 reviews, scoring 8.6. Real reviews love the thatched teak bungalows scattered through the valley, ringed by rice fields and a stream, with a clear eco, blend-into-nature ethos. It suits travellers who want a peaceful nature stay in Mae Hong Son rather than in-town convenience, from ฿1,500.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a Deluxe Stream View with a balcony over the stream for the full atmosphere · It's in the valley outskirts, so you'll want wheels and some mosquito repellent for the natural setting.
pros: Well reviewed with 602 reviews, strong nature setting
Teak bungalows in a valley ringed by rice fields and a stream
Eco-minded, blended into Mae Hong Son's nature
Great for a peaceful getaway from the bustle
cons: In the valley outskirts — you'll want wheels for town
It's in nature, so expect insects — pack repellent

entries.name: Baan Pai Riverside
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Pai River · Pai town
entries.addr: 190 Moo 1, Mae Hi, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: Baan Pai Riverside is a set of timber bungalows on the Pai River in town, from just ฿500, scoring 8.4 from 169 reviews. Real reviews like the central riverside location within walking distance of the walking street, and the simple timber-bungalow feel by the river. There are budget fan bungalows and air-con options, making it a fit for backpackers who want a riverside stay on a tight budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pay a touch more for a River View Fan bungalow to get a balcony over the river — better value · In the hot season, go for the Deluxe Air-con · It's a simple stay, all about location and price.
pros: Central riverside Pai location, walkable
Very low starter price of ฿500
Bungalows on the Pai River with a laid-back feel
Both fan and air-con bungalows available
cons: Simple timber bungalows with basic amenities
Starter rooms are fan-only, no air-con

entries.name: Spicypai Backpackers
entries.badge: 🎋 Bamboo dorms in the rice fields
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pai outskirts · in the rice fields
tags: 🌾 In the rice fields, mountain views
entries.addr: 291 Moo 1, Mae Yen, Mae Hi, Pai · Mae Hong Son
entries.storyHtml: Spicypai is the cheapest stay in this guide — bamboo-hut dorms in the rice fields from just ฿300, scoring 8.2 from 205 reviews. Real reviews love the hand-built, open-air bamboo huts set among the rice fields with mountain views, waking up to nature, and the backpacker vibe where you meet fellow travellers. It's for genuine backpackers who don't mind roughing it for the experience of sleeping in the fields on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: These are open-air bamboo huts, so pack warm layers in the cool season — Pai nights get cold · For a bit more privacy, try the private bamboo hut.
pros: Cheapest in this guide at ฿300
Hand-built bamboo-hut dorms in the rice fields with mountain views
Backpacker vibe, easy to meet fellow travellers
Wake up to full-on nature views
cons: Open-air bamboo huts get very cold in the cool season — pack warm layers
On the outskirts in the rice fields — you'll want wheels for the walking street

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Mae Hong Son & Pai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay in Pai or Mae Hong Son town?
faq.a: It depends on your trip · Pai suits anyone who loves a laid-back little town with a walking street, cafes and stays at every level (Pai Village, The Quarter, Pai Country Hut) · Mae Hong Son town is quieter, set in the mountains, better for a peaceful nature stay (Fern Resort, Sang Tong Huts) · The two are about 3 hours apart on a winding road, so with limited time pick one base.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Mae Hong Son and Pai hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and riverside bungalows start around ฿300–700/night · quality 3–4 star boutiques and resorts run about ฿1,000–1,800 · a 5-star luxury resort on the Pai River starts around ฿4,800 · In the cool season (Nov–Jan), which is high season, prices can run higher and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Mae Hong Son or Pai hotel?
faq.a: For weekdays outside the busy season, 2–4 weeks ahead is fine · But in the cool season (November–January) and over long weekends, Pai and Mae Hong Son town are high season and the good places fill fast — book 1–2 months ahead, especially for riverside resorts in Pai.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a vehicle for Mae Hong Son and Pai?
faq.a: In Pai town you can walk the walking street easily, but to head out of town or travel between Pai and Mae Hong Son town (over 1,800 curves, around 3 hours), you should rent a car or motorbike · Daily minivans run from Chiang Mai to both Pai and the town · Public transport within town is limited, so renting is easiest.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Mae Hong Son and Pai hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion at any given time, so it's worth opening all 3 to compare before you book — every review page in this guide has the price-comparison links, and you can save several hundred baht a night.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Mae Hong Son and Pai?
faq.a: The cool season (November–February) brings comfortable weather and lovely sea-of-mist mornings — the most popular but also the busiest and priciest window · February–March can bring haze from agricultural burning, so check the air quality first · The rainy season is lush and green but the mountain roads get slippery, so drive carefully.
